summary: GL-101 and GL-204 are both Approved glossary entries titled 'Settlement Date' but define different things. GL-101 (v1.0, owner Avery Example (SYNTHETIC)) defines it as the date cash and securities are actually exchanged to complete a trade (an actual/occurred event). GL-204 (v2.1, owner Blake Example (SYNTHETIC)) defines it as the contractual date by which payment and delivery must complete, as agreed at execution (an agreed/due date). The two are not equivalent: an actual exchange date can differ from the contractual due date (for example on a late or failed settlement). The glossary also records GL-101 as a CDE (recorded_cde_flag true) and GL-204 as not a CDE (false), and links the pair as possible_duplicate. Internal sources conflict, so I surface both and do not pick one; resolution is routed to the human Data Steward. This agent has not approved, finalised, assigned an owner to, or set CDE status on anything.
